name: Chip supply
summary: Nexperia and STMicro warn AI demand is squeezing mature-chip supply for carmakers; no TSMC or Samsung stoppage
state: At the Electronica fair in Munich on 9–10 Nov, Nexperia's interim chief executive said the company was 'totally oversubscribed' and STMicroelectronics' chief executive said he saw 'many bottlenecks', as suppliers shift capacity towards AI data centres and away from mature chips used in cars and industrial equipment (Reuters via The Star, 10 Nov). Reported shortages in a key segment keep this at Watch; no TSMC or Samsung stoppage and no new controls halting a major supply chain were found as of 13 Nov.
for_you: Car and industrial equipment makers are most exposed; mature-chip shortages tend to show up as longer lead times, production slowdowns and delayed vehicle deliveries rather than shortages of phones or computers.
rubric_hit: Watch: shortages reported in a key segment (mature automotive chips, 10 Nov); no major TSMC/Samsung disruption

sources.title: The Star (Reuters) — Chipmakers warn AI demand is creating bottlenecks in automotive supply chain

why: Advanced chips underpin everything from phones to AI to weapons; supply is concentrated in Taiwan and Korea.
drivers: Export controls, Taiwan risk, fab outages, AI demand, materials.

rubric.alert: Major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output, or controls halting a major supply chain.
rubric.watch: New export controls, shortages reported in key segments, or a fab outage.
rubric.normal: Supply normal; no new major controls.
